This case arise out of charge-sheet filed by the CID (EOW) P.S against the accused No.1 to 6 for the offence punishable U/s.420, 465, 468, 471, 409 R/w.Sec.34 of IPC.

Thereafter accused No.2 being FDA and accused No.3 being Chief Accountant of Education Department, Accounts Section, approved said bill without verification and forwarded it to cheque section.

Thus the accused No.4 in furtherance of common intention of all accused assisted accused No.1 to illegally draw aforesaid amount and accused No.1 during creating the aforesaid salary bill of aforesaid school forged signature of CW.12 the then BEO, Malleshwaram North Zone - I, in furtherance of common intention of all accused to cheat the Exchequer (Government), she presented said salary bill to concerned treasury as genuine,

to her account by taking cheque issued by their office and the accused No.4 being the then SDA of concerned treasury issued the aforesaid cheque to accused No.1 without effecting necessary entries in concerned registers in furtherance of common intention of all accused person for the benefit of accused No.1 and thereby he i.e., accused No.4 being public servant of treasury department committed criminal breach of trust.
In pursuance of the complaint I.O has filed charge-sheet against accused No.1 to 6 and for the aforesaid offences.

3. The accused No.4 is on bail and represented by his counsel, after complying with the provision of Sec.207 of Cr.P.C., and on hearing both sides, charge was framed, read- C.C.No.13956/2009 over and explained to the accused for which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

proclamation, rest of the prosecution witnesses have not secured.
Hence, the predecessor of this court after granted sufficient opportunities, evidence of said witnesses orders to be dropped.
5. The statement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C., was recorded, read over, explained to the accused No.4 for which he pleaded not guilty and denied the incriminating circumstances which appeared against him.

The following points do arise for my consideration:-
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that on accused No.1/R.Uma was working as Head Mistress in Vani Vidhya School of Laggere and though she did not belong to Sri.Vijayalakshmi Vidhya Kendra of Lakshminarayanapura, Bengaluru in the month of February 2000, she created fake salary bill of Rs.31,386/- on 09.03.2000 in respect of salary of aforesaid school by forging the signature of CW.12, then BEO of Malleshwaram North Zone-I and she submitted the bill to District Treasury of encashment.

which was later encashed by accused No.1 by presenting in her account No.11721 of Karnataka Bank,
Srirampur on 21.03.2000 and thereby she utilized aforesaid amount illegally for her personal again.
Thus the accused No.4 in furtherance of common intention of all accused assisted accused No.1 to illegally draw aforesaid amount and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.420 R/w.Sec.34 of IPC ?
2.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that accused No.1 during creating of aforesaid salary bills of aforesaid C.C.No.13956/2009 school forged the signature of CW.12 the then BEO, Malleshwaram North Zone - I and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.465 R/w.Sec.34 of IPC?

Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that accused No.1 during creating of aforesaid salary bill of aforesaid school forged signature of CW.12 the then BEO, Malleshwaram North Zone - I in furtherance of common intention of all accused to cheat the Exchequer (Government) and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.468 R/w.Sec.34 of IPC?
4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that accused No.1 by creating of salary bills of school forged signature of CW.12 the then BEO, Malleshwaram North Zone - I, in furtherance of common intention of all accused to cheat the Exchequer (Government) and she presented said salary bills to concerned treasury as genuine knowing fully well that it was a forged one and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.471 R/w.Sec.34 of IPC?

On careful perusal of the entire oral and documentary evidence and arguments addressed by the counsels the admitted facts are that there is no dispute that the present case is pending only against accused No.4, that too PW.1/Thirunavakkarasu in his evidence stated that he opened Meghanatha Educational Society and accused No.1 was the sole teacher of said school in 1993 and he received letters from the SBI, RKD Finance, B.K Co-Operative Society and other banks for non-payment of personal loan of nearly 20 persons.

33.

PW.21 - Sadananda Shivarama Padolakar who is also one of the part investigation officer, he also stated that about the receipts of records dated :06.11.2002 and written of letters to the banks, AG office, Treasuries and Karnataka bank to furnish documents and also received statements.

34. PW.22 - Shivanna who is part investigation officer stated that about receipts of records from CW.34 and visiting to the Karnataka Bank, Srirampura and receipts of records over the cheque No.36181 and 36901 and FSL report etc., C.C.No.13956/2009 35.

On perusal of the evidence of PW.1 to PW.22 out of these witnesses PW.17 to PW.22 they all are police witnesses, that too they are investigation officers, they simply stated before the court with regard to written of letters to the treasury and various banks to furnish records over the alleged transactions of Vani Vidya Kendra School, that too they have not stated any incriminating evidence against accused No.4.
36.

As stated supra on perusal of overall evidence of PW.1 to PW.22 and on perusal of Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.35 documents confers to the court that about drawing of double bills by the accused No.1 and further except PW.14 non of the witnesses have not stated any incriminating evidence against the accused No.4.

That too against accused No.4, PW.14 stated that about his role in Treasury and non entering of entries in KTC-66 register, except this lapses as well as dereliction of duties by the Smt. Vijayalakshmi vs R.Uma on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81993534/
7 accused No.4 about non entries in concerned register.
There is no other allegations with regard to the involvement of accused No.4 along with other accused in the alleged crime.
i.e., forging of documents for drawing of double salaries as per the charge-sheet materials.
Of course the prosecution has examined near 22 witnesses and exhibited 35 documents, but they are all not sufficient to believe the guilt C.C.No.13956/2009 against the accused No.4.

Because the said evidence only pertaining to the other accused not against accused No.4.
37

. Further even in the charge sheet materials and charge also, the allegation against accused No.4 is he is being Second Division Assistant of the concerned treasury, has hand over the cheques to accused No.1 without making entries in KTC-66, except this lapses there is no other materials placed against accused No.4 in this case about his dishonest intention and forging of bills as well as cheques to draw the double salaries and also using of said documents as genuine one and causing of misappropriation as well as criminal breach of trust.

So, in the absence of materials merely investigation officers have included the accused No.4 in this case and filed charge sheet in random manner against all accused are all not sufficient to convict the accused No.4 in this case.
38. As stated supra the case against accused No.5 and 6 has been quashed and accused No.1 to 3 have been died and case against them was abated.
Only this case is pending against accused No.4.

So except evidence against the accused No.1 and others, there is no direct evidence against accused No.4 and there is no corroborative, cogent and convincing evidence to believe the guilt against accused pertaining to the alleged sections.
As stated supra and as argued by the accused C.C.No.13956/2009 counsel except PW.14 evidence, that too about non entries in KTC-66 register by the accused No.4.
There is no other incriminating evidence has placed in this case.
39. Accordingly any amount of arguments addressed by the Ld.APP as stated supra have not support the prosecution case in any manner.
On the other hand as argued by the accused counsel except PW.14 evidence non of the witnesses have stated any incriminating evidence against the accused No.4.
That too PW.14 evidence is needs to be corroboration.

40. Further as stated supra non of the prosecution witness have identified the accused No.4 and stated about irresponsibility for drawing of double salaries as per the charge sheet materials by forging the documents and using the said documents as genuine and also causing of criminal breach of trust as per the alleged sections.

Accordingly any amount of arguments addressed by the Ld.APP and evidence placed by the prosecution including oral and documentary evidence are not sufficient to believe the guilt against the accused No.4.
Accordingly, I am of the opinion that prosecution has miserably failed to prove it's case beyond reasonable doubt as per the ingredients of allege sections.
Hence, I am of the opinion that accused No.4 is entitled for benefit of doubt as he C.C.No.13956/2009 has not found guilty.

Hence, my answer on points No.1 to 5 in the NEGATIVE.
41.
Point No.6
: From the discussions on foregoing points, this court opined that prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused No.4 punishable under the alleged sections of Penal Code.

Therefore, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER Accused No.4 is not found guilty.
